result.title: Smooth Essential-Manifold Residuals for View-Graph Calibration
result.summary: View-graph calibration jointly estimates camera intrinsics from multiple pairwise fundamental matrices. The correct intrinsics transform each fundamental matrix into an essential matrix, casting the calibration problem as minimizing the distance to the essential manifold. We study how to represent this objective for nonlinear least squares. The conventional singular-value formulation collapses two independent essential-matrix constraints into one scalar residual. Its per-edge Gauss-Newton model is therefore rank deficient, which leads to poor convergence. We instead derive an isometric reduction to 2x2 matrices, where each branch of the nonlinear essential-matrix constraint becomes a linear subspace. This reduction yields a smooth two-dimensional residual whose squared norm is exactly the original manifold distance, whose Gauss-Newton approximation is generically full rank, and whose evaluation requires no per-edge singular value decomposition. Experiments show that the new residual retains the estimation accuracy of the geometric objective while converging in fewer, computationally cheaper iterations. Combined with robust initialization and optimization, it achieves state-of-the-art view-graph calibration accuracy at a runtime comparable to inexpensive algebraic objectives.

AI.brief_summary: 研究 view-graph 标定中到 essential manifold 距离的目标表示，提出等距降维到 2×2 矩阵的平滑二维残差，使 Gauss-Newton 近似满秩且免去逐边 SVD，从而以更少、更省算的迭代收敛。
AI.relevance_reason: 其把几何约束改写为平滑、满秩的低维残差，可能为 LVR 中几何一致性的训练目标或 latent 几何量表示设计提供可供核查的线索，但论文本身不涉及视觉推理状态，与主线距离较远。
